records.title: Found by: bench (`python/docstring-unicode-escape`, `python/poison-escapes`).
records.description: Found by: bench (`python/docstring-unicode-escape`, `python/poison-escapes`). Python strings read `\uXXXX` as the letters `uXXXX` and did not decode `\xHH`, `\UXXXXXXXX` or octal (docstrings, `description=` and `name=` alike), so bidi, zero-width, tag and ANSI characters written as escapes never reached the poisoning checks, and `lookup_\u0430ccount` came out as `lookup_u0430ccount` (homoglyph missed, phantom name). Escapes are now decoded as Python decodes them; an unknown escape keeps its backslash; raw strings stay raw. Review follow-up: in a raw f-string a backslash no longer hides a `{expression}`.

test.name: R-RD-07: Python string escapes are decoded as Python decodes them (\x, \u, \U, octal); an unknown escape keeps its backslash

R-RD-07: a name= keyword is decoded, so a look-alike letter written as an escape is the name the server lists
R-RD-07: in a raw f-string a backslash stays and does not hide a {expression}

records.title: Found by: bench (`typescript/loop-over-definitions`).
records.description: Found by: bench (`typescript/loop-over-definitions`). `for (const t of TOOLS) server.registerTool(t.name, …)` reported one unresolved registration even though every name in `TOOLS` was read. Registrations in a loop over a literal or constant collection read in full are now read once per element; a loop over anything else still counts as unresolved. R-RD-15: a loop over a collection the reader does not know in full still counts its registration as unresolved
R-RD-15: a collection that is changed after its declaration (push, let reassigned, index assignment) is not unrolled; its registration stays unresolved
R-RD-15: a parameter or an outer loop variable that shadows a constant is not read as the constant
R-RD-15: an index expression before .forEach is not an array literal, and a loop body that may skip the registration is not unrolled
R-RD-15: many loops and factory calls next to many constants are read in linear time

records.title: **Finding (containment):** a target's work volume had no disk or inode cap.
records.description: **Finding (containment):** a target's work volume had no disk or inode cap. Named Docker volumes sat on the runner's own disk, so an install or server that wrote without end (an archive bomb, a fill, one `fallocate`) could fill it, and with it the shard's results and the targets after it. `install-runsc.sh` now mounts Docker's volumes folder as an ext4 file of its own (`volume_fs_mb` 6144, `volume_fs_inodes` 1,048,576 in `gvisor.json`, reserved up front and formatted with `nodiscard` so the reservation holds, mounted before any volume exists), and the strict preflight refuses a host without it. A first version formatted it with the default discard, which punched holes through the reservation: on GitHub the bomb filled the capped volume yet the runner's disk still lost 2069 MB. Found by R-CASE-21's mutation (`volume-cap`), which runs the case on a volume that is not on that filesystem.

records.description: Pulled target images had no disk cap: a layer that unpacks without end would fill the runner's disk. Docker's whole data-root now lives on a filesystem of its own (`docker_root` /var/lib/isokron-docker, `docker_fs_mb` 20480, `docker_fs_inodes` 2,097,152, reserved up front), with the volumes filesystem (R-SBX-23) inside it, and the containerd image store pinned off so images stay on it (overlay2). The strict preflight checks the data-root, overlay2, both filesystems' inode counts, and that each image file is fully reserved (no holes: a discard or a trim would hand its blocks back); fstrim's timer is stopped. On GitHub the first version lost 512 MB of the data-root's reservation within seconds, which the hole check caught: it was the inode tables, which the kernel's lazy init zeroes after the mount with write-zeroes requests that a loop device turns into holes. mkfs now writes the inode tables and journal itself (`lazy_itable_init=0,lazy_journal_init=0`); both are also mounted `nodiscard`, and the preflight refuses one mounted with discard. From the review of pull request 11.
